svg.title: Scenario-conditioned diffusion transformer architecture
svg.desc: Editable reconstruction of the full architecture diagram. Major base frames: scenario inputs at upper left, encoder upper center, decoder upper right, denoising-step column at far right, and the large lower diffusion block. Inventoried contents include map-like scene panels with lanes, vehicles and agents; small input crops for neighbors, navigation, lanes and static objects; MLP-Mixer and MLP blocks; Self-Attention stack; decoder condition token, diffusion transformer and timestep; denoising snapshots over time; and a lower transformer denoising pipeline with conditioning arrows and module blocks. Overall symmetry is a left-to-right encoder/decoder flow with a lower horizontally partitioned denoising transformer, while the right column is vertically equipartitioned into four temporal snapshots.

g.desc: Scenario-input frame contains a large scene map at left, three stacked local crops for neighbors/navigation, and two middle crops for lanes/static objects. Directional flow proceeds from Scene to neighbor/navigation crops, then to lane/static-object crops, then rightward into the encoder.

Encoder frame has three horizontally aligned feature mixers on the left and a tall Self-Attention repeated block at right; outputs from Scenario Inputs enter the three left modules and merge through attention.
Decoder frame receives encoded scenario condition through a small token, a diamond/connection, and a Diffusion Transformer box; its lower output feeds the large denoising block.

Right column displays four successive denoising snapshots stacked vertically under a downward time arrow t. Each snapshot is a cropped map-like scene containing green point cloud, lanes, navy vehicles, and orange target agent.

Lower diffusion block progresses horizontally from noisy state x(t), through state-constraint and neighbor inputs, repeated transformer layers with LN, Scale Shift, Scale, FFN and Multi-Head Attention blocks, then a final layer and output x(t-delta t). Top condition arrows drop into scale-related blocks; a bottom scenario-condition arrow feeds the model.
